```{r cleaning columns name}
colnames(stress_survey_data) = colnames(stress_survey_data) %>%
  tolower() %>%
  str_replace_all(" ", "_") %>%                    # Spaces to underscores
  str_replace_all("\\(|\\)", "") %>%               # Remove parentheses
  str_replace_all("-", "_") %>%                    # Hyphens to underscores
  str_replace_all("__+", "_") %>%                  # Multiple underscores to single
  str_remove("_$")           

colnames(stress_survey_data)

```

```{r data type conversion}

stress_survey_data = stress_survey_data %>%
  mutate(
    gender = as.factor(gender),
    stress_coping_mechanisms = as.factor(stress_coping_mechanisms),
    
    # Binary variables (adjust based on your actual coding)
    counseling_attendance = as.factor(counseling_attendance),
    family_mental_health_history = as.factor(family_mental_health_history),
    medical_condition = as.factor(medical_condition),
    
    # Ensure numeric variables are numeric
    age = as.numeric(age),
    academic_performance_gpa = as.numeric(academic_performance_gpa),
    study_hours_per_week = as.numeric(study_hours_per_week),
    social_media_usage_hours_per_day = as.numeric(social_media_usage_hours_per_day),
    sleep_duration_hours_per_night = as.numeric(sleep_duration_hours_per_night),
    physical_exercise_hours_per_week = as.numeric(physical_exercise_hours_per_week),
    family_support = as.numeric(family_support),
    financial_stress = as.numeric(financial_stress),
    peer_pressure = as.numeric(peer_pressure),
    relationship_stress = as.numeric(relationship_stress),
    mental_stress_level = as.numeric(mental_stress_level),
    diet_quality = as.numeric(diet_quality),
    cognitive_distortions = as.numeric(cognitive_distortions),

  )
```

```{r EDA stress vs. continuous variable}

# Correlation analysis
numeric_df = stress_survey_data %>%
  select(where(is.numeric), -student_id)

correlation_matrix <- cor(numeric_df, use = "complete.obs")

# Extract correlations with mental_stress_level
stress_correlations = correlation_matrix["mental_stress_level", ] %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "variable") %>%
  rename(correlation = 2) %>%
  filter(variable != "mental_stress_level") %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(correlation)))

print(stress_correlations)

# Visualize correlations with mental stress level
ggplot(stress_correlations, aes(x = reorder(variable, correlation), y = correlation, 
                                 fill = correlation > 0)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "steelblue")) +
  labs(title = "Correlation of Variables with Mental Stress Level",
       x = "Variable",
       y = "Correlation Coefficient") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

#heatmap
install.packages("corrplot")
library(corrplot)
corrplot(correlation_matrix, method = "color", type = "upper", 
          tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45, tl.cex = 0.7)

# Scatter plots for top correlated variables
top_vars = stress_correlations %>%
  slice_max(abs(correlation), n = 6) %>%
  pull(variable)

stress_survey_data %>%
  select(mental_stress_level, all_of(top_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-mental_stress_level, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = mental_stress_level)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(title = "Mental Stress Level vs. Top Correlated Variables",
       x = "Variable Value",
       y = "Mental Stress Level") +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r association rule mining}

install.packages("arules")
install.packages("arulesViz")

library(arules)

df_discretized = stress_survey_data %>%
  mutate(
    age_group = cut(age, breaks = c(17, 20, 23, 30), 
                    labels = c("18-20", "21-23", "24+"),
                    include.lowest = TRUE),
    gpa_level = cut(academic_performance_gpa, breaks = quantile(academic_performance_gpa, probs = c(0, 0.33, 0.67, 1)), #to get 0
                    labels = c("Low_GPA", "Medium_GPA", "High_GPA"), include.lowest = TRUE),
    study_hours = cut(study_hours_per_week, breaks = c(-0.01, 10, 20, 50), 
                      labels = c("Low_Study", "Medium_Study", "High_Study")),
    social_media = cut(social_media_usage_hours_per_day, breaks = c(-0.01, 2, 5, 24), 
                       labels = c("Low_SocialMedia", "Medium_SocialMedia", "High_SocialMedia")),
    sleep_quality = cut(sleep_duration_hours_per_night, breaks = c(-0.01, 6, 8, 12), 
                        labels = c("Poor_Sleep", "Good_Sleep", "Excellent_Sleep")),
    exercise_level = cut(physical_exercise_hours_per_week, breaks = c(-0.01, 2, 5, 20), 
                         labels = c("Low_Exercise", "Medium_Exercise", "High_Exercise")),
    family_support_level = cut(family_support, breaks = c(0, 2, 4, 5), 
                               labels = c("Low_Support", "Medium_Support", "High_Support")),
    financial_stress_level = cut(financial_stress, breaks = c(0, 2, 4, 5), 
                                  labels = c("Low_FinStress", "Medium_FinStress", "High_FinStress")),
    peer_pressure_level = cut(peer_pressure, breaks = c(0, 2, 4, 5), 
                              labels = c("Low_PeerPress", "Medium_PeerPress", "High_PeerPress")),
    relationship_stress_level = cut(relationship_stress, breaks = c(0, 2, 4, 5), 
                                    labels = c("Low_RelStress", "Medium_RelStress", "High_RelStress")),
    diet_level = cut(diet_quality, breaks = c(0, 2, 4, 5), 
                     labels = c("Poor_Diet", "Medium_Diet", "Good_Diet")),
    cognitive_distortions_level = cut(cognitive_distortions, breaks = c(0, 2, 4, 5), 
                                       labels = c("Low_CogDist", "Medium_CogDist", "High_CogDist")),
    substance_use_level = cut(substance_use, breaks = c(0, 1, 3, 5), 
                              labels = c("No_Substance", "Low_Substance", "High_Substance"))
  )
# Verify no NAs were created
colSums(is.na(df_discretized))

# Select relevant columns for association rules
df_for_rules = df_discretized %>%
  select(stress_category, stress_coping_mechanisms, age_group, gender,
         gpa_level, study_hours, social_media, sleep_quality, exercise_level,
         family_support_level, financial_stress_level, peer_pressure_level,
         relationship_stress_level, diet_level, cognitive_distortions_level,
         substance_use_level, counseling_attendance, family_mental_health_history,
         medical_condition)

# Convert to transaction format
transactions = as(df_for_rules, "transactions")

# Inspect transactions
summary(transactions)
inspect(head(transactions, 3))

```
```{r }

stress_rules = apriori(transactions,
                        parameter = list(supp = 0.005,  # Lower support threshold
                                       conf = 0.3,      # Lower confidence
                                       minlen = 2, 
                                       maxlen = 5),
                        appearance = list(
                          lhs = c("stress_category=Low",
                                  "stress_category=Medium",
                                  "stress_category=High"),
                          rhs = c("stress_coping_mechanisms=Exercise",
                                  "stress_coping_mechanisms=Meditation",
                                  "stress_coping_mechanisms=Reading",
                                  "stress_coping_mechanisms=Social Media Engagement",
                                  "stress_coping_mechanisms=Spending Time Alone",
                                  "stress_coping_mechanisms=Talking to Friends",
                                  "stress_coping_mechanisms=Travelling",
                                  "stress_coping_mechanisms=Walking or Nature Walks",
                                  "stress_coping_mechanisms=Watching Sports",
                                  "stress_coping_mechanisms=Yoga"),
                          default = "lhs"  # ⭐ CHANGED: Allow other items on LHS
                        ),
                        control = list(verbose = FALSE))

# Check how many rules
length(stress_rules)

# Inspect
stress_rules_sorted <- sort(stress_rules, by = "confidence", decreasing = TRUE)
inspect(head(stress_rules_sorted, 20))

stress_rules_df <- as(stress_rules_sorted, "data.frame")
head(stress_rules_df, 10)

```

```{r }
# View full rules with actual coping mechanism names
inspect(head(stress_rules_sorted, 20))

# Or extract the RHS (right-hand side)
stress_rules_df <- as(stress_rules_sorted, "data.frame")

stress_rules_df <- stress_rules_df %>%
  mutate(
    # Extract just the coping mechanism from RHS
    coping_mechanism = str_extract(rules, "stress_coping_mechanisms=([^}]+)"),
    coping_mechanism = str_remove(coping_mechanism, "stress_coping_mechanisms=")
  )

# View rules by coping mechanism
stress_rules_df %>%
  select(rules, coping_mechanism, support, confidence, lift, count) %>%
  arrange(desc(lift)) %>%
  head(20)

# Count which coping mechanisms appear most in high-lift rules
table(stress_rules_df$coping_mechanism[stress_rules_df$lift > 7])
```

### Build Multiple Regression Modeling 

```{r prepare data and build initial model}
install.packages("car")
library(car)        # For VIF (multicollinearity check)
library(caret)      # For model evaluation

set.seed(123)

# 1. Data preparation 

# Create train/test split (80/20)
train_index <- sample(1:nrow(stress_survey_data), 0.8 * nrow(stress_survey_data))
train_data <- stress_survey_data[train_index, ]
test_data <- stress_survey_data[-train_index, ]

cat("Training set size:", nrow(train_data), "\n")
cat("Testing set size:", nrow(test_data), "\n")

# Check class balance in train/test
cat("\nStress distribution in training set:\n")
table(train_data$stress_category)
cat("\nStress distribution in test set:\n")
table(test_data$stress_category)



```
```{r buid regression model}

model_full <- lm(mental_stress_level ~ 
                   age + 
                   gender + 
                   academic_performance_gpa + 
                   study_hours_per_week + 
                   social_media_usage_hours_per_day +
                   sleep_duration_hours_per_night + 
                   physical_exercise_hours_per_week +
                   family_support + 
                   financial_stress + 
                   peer_pressure +
                   relationship_stress + 
                   diet_quality + 
                   cognitive_distortions +
                   substance_use + 
                   counseling_attendance + 
                   family_mental_health_history + 
                   medical_condition +
                   stress_coping_mechanisms,
                 data = train_data)

# Summary
cat("\n========== FULL MODEL SUMMARY ==========\n")
summary(model_full)

# Extract significant predictors (p < 0.05)
cat("\n========== SIGNIFICANT PREDICTORS (p < 0.05) ==========\n")
sig_predictors <- summary(model_full)$coefficients[summary(model_full)$coefficients[,4] < 0.05, ]
print(sig_predictors)

```
```{r Check Model Assumption}

# 1. Diagnostic plots
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model_full, main = "Full Model Diagnostics")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# 2. Check for multicollinearity (VIF)
cat("\nVariance Inflation Factors (VIF):\n")
cat("(VIF > 10 indicates high multicollinearity)\n\n")

# Calculate VIF for numeric predictors only
vif_values <- vif(model_full)
print(vif_values)

# Identify problematic variables
high_vif <- vif_values[vif_values > 10]
if (length(high_vif) > 0) {
  cat("\n⚠️ HIGH MULTICOLLINEARITY detected in:\n")
  print(high_vif)
} else {
  cat("\n✅ No severe multicollinearity detected\n")
}

# 3. Test for normality of residuals
shapiro_test <- shapiro.test(residuals(model_full))
cat("\nShapiro-Wilk test for normality of residuals:\n")
cat("p-value:", shapiro_test$p.value, "\n")
if (shapiro_test$p.value < 0.05) {
  cat("⚠️ Residuals may not be normally distributed\n")
} else {
  cat("✅ Residuals appear normally distributed\n")
}

# ==========================================
# STEP 5.4: STEPWISE REGRESSION
# ==========================================

cat("\n========== STEPWISE VARIABLE SELECTION ==========\n")

# Perform stepwise selection (both directions)
model_step <- step(model_full, direction = "both", trace = 0)

cat("\nStepwise Model Summary:\n")
summary(model_step)

# Compare full vs stepwise model
cat("\n========== MODEL COMPARISON ==========\n")
anova(model_step, model_full)

# Extract final predictors in stepwise model
final_predictors <- names(coef(model_step))[-1]  # Remove intercept
cat("\nFinal predictors selected:\n")
print(final_predictors)

# ==========================================
# STEP 5.5: MODEL PERFORMANCE ON TEST SET
# ==========================================

cat("\n========== MODEL PERFORMANCE ==========\n")

# Predictions on test set - Full model
predictions_full <- predict(model_full, newdata = test_data)

# Predictions on test set - Stepwise model
predictions_step <- predict(model_step, newdata = test_data)

# Calculate performance metrics
evaluate_model <- function(actual, predicted, model_name) {
  rmse <- sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
  mae <- mean(abs(actual - predicted), na.rm = TRUE)
  r_squared <- cor(actual, predicted, use = "complete.obs")^2
  
  cat("\n", model_name, "Performance:\n")
  cat("  RMSE:", round(rmse, 3), "\n")
  cat("  MAE:", round(mae, 3), "\n")
  cat("  R-squared:", round(r_squared, 3), "\n")
  
  return(list(rmse = rmse, mae = mae, r_squared = r_squared))
}

perf_full <- evaluate_model(test_data$mental_stress_level, predictions_full, "Full Model")
perf_step <- evaluate_model(test_data$mental_stress_level, predictions_step, "Stepwise Model")
```

```{r analyzing feature}


cat("\n========== FEATURE IMPORTANCE ==========\n")

# Extract standardized coefficients for comparison
standardized_coef <- function(model) {
  # Get coefficients
  coefs <- coef(model)[-1]  # Remove intercept
  
  # Get predictor names
  pred_names <- names(coefs)
  
  # Standardize by absolute value
  importance <- abs(coefs)
  
  # Create dataframe
  importance_df <- data.frame(
    predictor = pred_names,
    coefficient = coefs,
    abs_coefficient = importance
  ) %>%
    arrange(desc(abs_coefficient))
  
  return(importance_df)
}

importance_step <- standardized_coef(model_step)
cat("\nTop 10 Most Important Predictors (by absolute coefficient):\n")
print(head(importance_step, 10))

# Visualize feature importance
importance_step_top <- head(importance_step, 15)

ggplot(importance_step_top, aes(x = reorder(predictor, abs_coefficient), 
                                 y = abs_coefficient,
                                 fill = coefficient > 0)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "steelblue"),
                    labels = c("Negative", "Positive"),
                    name = "Effect") +
  labs(title = "Feature Importance in Predicting Mental Stress",
       subtitle = "Top 15 predictors from stepwise regression",
       x = "Predictor",
       y = "Absolute Coefficient Value") +
  theme_minimal()

# ==========================================
# STEP 5.8: ANALYZE COPING MECHANISM EFFECTS
# ==========================================

cat("\n========== COPING MECHANISM EFFECTS ==========\n")

# Extract coping mechanism coefficients from model
coping_coefs <- coef(model_step)[grep("stress_coping_mechanisms", names(coef(model_step)))]

if (length(coping_coefs) > 0) {
  coping_effects <- data.frame(
    mechanism = gsub("stress_coping_mechanisms", "", names(coping_coefs)),
    coefficient = coping_coefs,
    effect = ifelse(coping_coefs < 0, "Reduces Stress", "Increases Stress")
  ) %>%
    arrange(coefficient)
  
  cat("\nCoping Mechanism Effects on Stress (relative to reference category):\n")
  print(coping_effects)
  
  # Visualize
  ggplot(coping_effects, aes(x = reorder(mechanism, coefficient), 
                              y = coefficient,
                              fill = effect)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Reduces Stress" = "green", 
                                  "Increases Stress" = "red")) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title = "Effect of Coping Mechanisms on Mental Stress",
         subtitle = "Negative coefficient = reduces stress (better)",
         x = "Coping Mechanism",
         y = "Coefficient (Effect on Stress Level)") +
    theme_minimal()
} else {
  cat("⚠️ Coping mechanisms were not retained in the stepwise model\n")
  cat("This suggests coping mechanisms don't have strong predictive power\n")
  cat("after controlling for other variables (likely due to reverse causality)\n")
}
```

```{r recommendation engine}

# ==========================================
# PART C: RECOMMENDATION ENGINE
# ==========================================

recommend_coping_strategies_CORRECTED <- function(student_profile, 
                                                   stress_rules_df,  # YOUR mined rules
                                                   model_step,
                                                   top_n = 3) {
  #' Generate personalized coping recommendations
  #' 
  #' @param student_profile: Single row dataframe with student data
  #' @param stress_rules_df: YOUR association rules from mining (with 'rules' and 'coping_mechanism' columns)
  #' @param model_step: Your trained regression model
  #' @param top_n: Number of recommendations to return
  #' 
  #' @return: Recommendations with rationale
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("ADAPTIVE STRESS-COPING RECOMMENDATION\n")
  cat("========================================\n\n")
  
  # -----------------------------------
  # STEP 1: PREDICT STRESS LEVEL
  # -----------------------------------
  
  predicted_stress <- predict(model_step, newdata = student_profile)
  
  stress_category <- case_when(
    predicted_stress <= 3 ~ "Low",
    predicted_stress <= 6 ~ "Medium",
    predicted_stress <= 10 ~ "High"
  )
  
  cat("STUDENT PROFILE ANALYSIS\n")
  cat("------------------------\n")
  cat("Predicted Mental Stress Level:", round(predicted_stress, 2), "/10\n")
  cat("Stress Category:", stress_category, "\n\n")
  
  # -----------------------------------
  # STEP 2: CREATE DISCRETIZED PROFILE FOR RULE MATCHING
  # -----------------------------------
  
  # This matches the discretization used in YOUR rule mining
  student_discrete <- data.frame(
    age_group = as.character(cut(student_profile$age, 
                                  breaks = c(17, 20, 23, 30), 
                                  labels = c("18-20", "21-23", "24+"), 
                                  include.lowest = TRUE)),
    
    gender = as.character(student_profile$gender),
    
    gpa_level = case_when(
      student_profile$academic_performance_gpa <= 1.33 ~ "Low_GPA",
      student_profile$academic_performance_gpa <= 2.67 ~ "Medium_GPA",
      TRUE ~ "High_GPA"
    ),
    
    study_hours = case_when(
      student_profile$study_hours_per_week <= 10 ~ "Low_Study",
      student_profile$study_hours_per_week <= 20 ~ "Medium_Study",
      TRUE ~ "High_Study"
    ),
    
    social_media = case_when(
      student_profile$social_media_usage_hours_per_day <= 2 ~ "Low_SocialMedia",
      student_profile$social_media_usage_hours_per_day <= 5 ~ "Medium_SocialMedia",
      TRUE ~ "High_SocialMedia"
    ),
    
    sleep_quality = case_when(
      student_profile$sleep_duration_hours_per_night < 6 ~ "Poor_Sleep",
      student_profile$sleep_duration_hours_per_night <= 8 ~ "Good_Sleep",
      TRUE ~ "Excellent_Sleep"
    ),
    
    exercise_level = case_when(
      student_profile$physical_exercise_hours_per_week <= 2 ~ "Low_Exercise",
      student_profile$physical_exercise_hours_per_week <= 5 ~ "Medium_Exercise",
      TRUE ~ "High_Exercise"
    ),
    
    family_support_level = case_when(
      student_profile$family_support <= 2 ~ "Low_Support",
      student_profile$family_support <= 4 ~ "Medium_Support",
      TRUE ~ "High_Support"
    ),
    
    financial_stress_level = case_when(
      student_profile$financial_stress <= 2 ~ "Low_FinStress",
      student_profile$financial_stress <= 4 ~ "Medium_FinStress",
      TRUE ~ "High_FinStress"
    ),
    
    peer_pressure_level = case_when(
      student_profile$peer_pressure <= 2 ~ "Low_PeerPress",
      student_profile$peer_pressure <= 4 ~ "Medium_PeerPress",
      TRUE ~ "High_PeerPress"
    ),
    
    relationship_stress_level = case_when(
      student_profile$relationship_stress <= 2 ~ "Low_RelStress",
      student_profile$relationship_stress <= 4 ~ "Medium_RelStress",
      TRUE ~ "High_RelStress"
    ),
    
    stress_category = stress_category
  )
  
  cat("Discretized student profile created for rule matching\n\n")
  
  # -----------------------------------
  # STEP 3: MATCH RULES TO STUDENT PROFILE
  # -----------------------------------
  
  cat("MATCHING ASSOCIATION RULES...\n")
  cat("------------------------\n")
  
  # Add match score to each rule
  stress_rules_df$match_score <- 0
  stress_rules_df$matching_conditions <- ""
  
  for (i in 1:nrow(stress_rules_df)) {
    rule_lhs <- stress_rules_df$rules[i]
    
    matches <- 0
    total_conditions <- 0
    matching_list <- c()
    
    # Check each discretized attribute
    for (attr_name in names(student_discrete)) {
      attr_value <- student_discrete[[attr_name]]
      
      # Create the pattern to search for (e.g., "age_group=18-20")
      pattern <- paste0(attr_name, "=", attr_value)
      
      # Check if this pattern appears in the rule
      if (grepl(pattern, rule_lhs, fixed = TRUE)) {
        matches <- matches + 1
        matching_list <- c(matching_list, pattern)
      }
      
      # Count if this attribute appears at all in the rule
      if (grepl(attr_name, rule_lhs)) {
        total_conditions <- total_conditions + 1
      }
    }
    
    # Calculate match score
    if (total_conditions > 0) {
      stress_rules_df$match_score[i] <- matches / total_conditions
      stress_rules_df$matching_conditions[i] <- paste(matching_list, collapse = ", ")
    }
  }
  
  # Filter for rules that match the student
  matched_rules <- stress_rules_df %>%
    filter(match_score > 0.5) %>%  # At least 50% of conditions match
    arrange(desc(match_score), desc(lift), desc(confidence))
  
  cat("Found", nrow(matched_rules), "rules matching this student profile\n")
  
  # If no good matches, fall back to top rules by lift
  if (nrow(matched_rules) < top_n) {
    cat("⚠️  Limited matches - including high-lift rules as backup\n")
    
    backup_rules <- stress_rules_df %>%
      filter(!rules %in% matched_rules$rules) %>%  # Don't duplicate
      arrange(desc(lift)) %>%
      head(top_n - nrow(matched_rules))
    
    matched_rules <- bind_rows(matched_rules, backup_rules)
  }
  
  cat("\n")
  
  # -----------------------------------
  # STEP 4: IDENTIFY STRESS DRIVERS
  # -----------------------------------
  
  cat("PRIMARY STRESS DRIVERS:\n")
cat("------------------------\n")

# Create a comprehensive list of all potential stress factors with scores
all_stress_factors <- data.frame(
  factor_name = character(),
  factor_value = numeric(),
  severity = character(),
  icon = character(),
  description = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 1. Financial Stress
if (!is.na(student_profile$financial_stress)) {
  all_stress_factors <- rbind(all_stress_factors, data.frame(
    factor_name = "Financial Stress",
    factor_value = student_profile$financial_stress,
    severity = case_when(
      student_profile$financial_stress >= 4 ~ "HIGH",
      student_profile$financial_stress >= 3 ~ "MODERATE",
      TRUE ~ "LOW"
    ),
    icon = case_when(
      student_profile$financial_stress >= 4 ~ "🔴",
      student_profile$financial_stress >= 3 ~ "🟡",
      TRUE ~ "🟢"
    ),
    description = paste0(student_profile$financial_stress, "/5")
  ))
}

# 2. Peer Pressure
if (!is.na(student_profile$peer_pressure)) {
  all_stress_factors <- rbind(all_stress_factors, data.frame(
    factor_name = "Peer Pressure",
    factor_value = student_profile$peer_pressure,
    severity = case_when(
      student_profile$peer_pressure >= 4 ~ "HIGH",
      student_profile$peer_pressure >= 3 ~ "MODERATE",

    ),
    icon = case_when(

      student_profile$peer_pressure >= 3 ~ "🟡",
      TRUE ~ "🟢"
    ),
    description = paste0(student_profile$peer_pressure, "/5")
  ))
}

# 3. Relationship Stress
if (!is.na(student_profile$relationship_stress)) {
  all_stress_factors <- rbind(all_stress_factors, data.frame(
    factor_name = "Relationship Stress",
    factor_value = student_profile$relationship_stress,
    severity = case_when(
      student_profile$relationship_stress >= 4 ~ "HIGH",
      student_profile$relationship_stress >= 3 ~ "MODERATE",

    ),
    icon = case_when(

    description = paste0(student_profile$relationship_stress, "/5")

# 4. Cognitive Distortions

  all_stress_factors <- rbind(all_stress_factors, data.frame(
    factor_name = "Cognitive Distortions",
    factor_value = student_profile$cognitive_distortions,
    severity = case_when(
      student_profile$cognitive_distortions >= 4 ~ "HIGH",

# 6. Family Support (inverse: low support = high stress)

    factor_name = "Sedentary Lifestyle",
    factor_value = exercise_stress_score,
    severity = case_when(
      exercise_stress_score >= 4 ~ "HIGH",
      exercise_stress_score >= 3 ~ "MODERATE",
      TRUE ~ "LOW"
    ),
    icon = case_when(
      exercise_stress_score >= 4 ~ "🔴",
      exercise_stress_score >= 3 ~ "🟡",
      TRUE ~ "🟢"
    ),
    description = paste0(student_profile$physical_exercise_hours_per_week, " hrs/week exercise")
  ))
}

# 12. Poor Diet Quality
if (!is.na(student_profile$diet_quality)) {
  diet_stress_score <- 6 - student_profile$diet_quality  # Inverse scale
  
  all_stress_factors <- rbind(all_stress_factors, data.frame(
    factor_name = "Poor Diet",
    factor_value = diet_stress_score,
    severity = case_when(
      diet_stress_score >= 4 ~ "HIGH",
      diet_stress_score >= 3 ~ "MODERATE",
      TRUE ~ "LOW"
    ),
    icon = case_when(
      diet_stress_score >= 4 ~ "🔴",
      diet_stress_score >= 3 ~ "🟡",
      TRUE ~ "🟢"
    ),
    description = paste0("Diet quality: ", student_profile$diet_quality, "/5")
  ))
}

# Sort by severity and value
all_stress_factors <- all_stress_factors %>%
  mutate(
    severity_rank = case_when(
      severity == "HIGH" ~ 3,
      severity == "MODERATE" ~ 2,
      severity == "LOW" ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(severity_rank), desc(factor_value))

# Get top 7-8 factors (only those with at least MODERATE severity)
top_stress_factors <- all_stress_factors %>%
  filter(severity_rank >= 2) %>%  # MODERATE or HIGH only
  head(8)

# If fewer than 8 HIGH/MODERATE factors, include some LOW factors
if (nrow(top_stress_factors) < 8) {
  remaining_factors <- all_stress_factors %>%
    filter(severity_rank < 2) %>%
    head(8 - nrow(top_stress_factors))
  
  top_stress_factors <- bind_rows(top_stress_factors, remaining_factors)
}

# Display results
if (nrow(top_stress_factors) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("Identified %d stress factors (showing top %d):\n\n", 
              nrow(all_stress_factors), 
              min(8, nrow(top_stress_factors))))
  
  for (i in 1:nrow(top_stress_factors)) {
    factor <- top_stress_factors[i, ]
    
    cat(sprintf("  %s %-25s [%-8s] %s\n",
                factor$icon,
                factor$factor_name,
                factor$severity,
                factor$description))
  }
  
  # Summary by severity
  cat("\n")
  high_count <- sum(top_stress_factors$severity == "HIGH")
  moderate_count <- sum(top_stress_factors$severity == "MODERATE")
  low_count <- sum(top_stress_factors$severity == "LOW")
  
  cat(sprintf("  Summary: %d HIGH, %d MODERATE, %d LOW risk factors\n",
              high_count, moderate_count, low_count))
  
} else {
  cat("  ✅ No major stress drivers identified - you're managing well!\n")
}

cat("\n")

# Store for return value
stress_factors <- top_stress_factors
  
  # -----------------------------------
  # STEP 5: GENERATE TOP N RECOMMENDATIONS
  # -----------------------------------
  
  cat("========================================\n")
  cat("RECOMMENDED COPING STRATEGIES\n")
  cat("========================================\n\n")
  
  # Get unique mechanisms (in case multiple rules recommend same mechanism)
  unique_recommendations <- matched_rules %>%
    group_by(coping_mechanism) %>%
    summarise(
      best_lift = max(lift),
      best_confidence = max(confidence),
      best_match_score = max(match_score),
      total_evidence = sum(count),
      best_matching_conditions = first(matching_conditions[which.max(match_score)]),
      .groups = 'drop'
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      relevance_score = best_match_score * best_lift * best_confidence
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(relevance_score)) %>%
    head(top_n)
  
  recommendations <- list()
  
  for (i in 1:nrow(unique_recommendations)) {
    rec <- unique_recommendations[i, ]
    mechanism <- rec$coping_mechanism
    
    # Medal emoji
    medal <- c("🥇", "🥈", "🥉")[i]
    
    cat(medal, "RECOMMENDATION", i, ":", mechanism, "\n")
    cat(strrep("-", 60), "\n")
    cat(sprintf("Confidence: %.0f%% | Effectiveness: %.1f× stronger | Match: %.0f%%\n",
                rec$best_confidence * 100,
                rec$best_lift,
                rec$best_match_score * 100))
    cat("\n")
    
    cat("Why this works for you:\n")
    cat("  • Based on", rec$total_evidence, "students with similar profiles\n")
    
    if (nchar(rec$best_matching_conditions) > 0) {
      cat("  • You match on:", rec$best_matching_conditions, "\n")
    }
    
    cat("  • Evidence from association rule mining\n")
    cat("\n")
    
    # Mechanism-specific guidance
    cat("How to implement:\n")
    
    if (mechanism == "Talking to Friends") {
      cat("  • Schedule 2-3 social activities per week\n")
      cat("  • Reach out to close friends for stress check-ins\n")
      cat("  • Join study groups for academic + social support\n")
      
    } else if (mechanism == "Exercise") {
      cat("  • Start with 15-20 minutes of walking daily\n")
      cat("  • Join campus fitness classes or sports clubs\n")
      cat("  • Gradually increase intensity over 2-4 weeks\n")
      cat("  ⚠️  Note: Benefits appear after 2-4 weeks of consistency\n")
      
    } else if (mechanism == "Walking or Nature Walks") {
      cat("  • Take 20-30 minute walks in green spaces daily\n")
      cat("  • Use walking as study breaks (every 50 minutes)\n")
      cat("  • Explore campus nature trails or nearby parks\n")
      
    } else if (mechanism == "Watching Sports") {
      cat("  • Watch favorite sports with friends (social + relaxation)\n")
      cat("  • Schedule viewing as reward after study sessions\n")
      cat("  • Join sports fan clubs on campus\n")
      
    } else if (mechanism == "Spending Time Alone") {
      cat("  • Schedule 30-60 minutes of quiet time daily\n")
      cat("  • Create a calm personal space for recharging\n")
      cat("  • Balance alone time with social activities\n")
      cat("  ⚠️  Note: Monitor for isolation - maintain some social contact\n")
      
    } else if (mechanism == "Reading") {
      cat("  • Set aside 30 min daily for leisure reading\n")
      cat("  • Choose engaging, positive content\n")
      cat("  • Join book clubs for social + reading benefits\n")
      
    } else if (mechanism == "Meditation") {
      cat("  • Start with 5-10 min guided meditation daily\n")
      cat("  • Use apps like Headspace, Calm, or Insight Timer\n")
      cat("  • Join campus meditation groups\n")
      
    } else if (mechanism == "Yoga") {
      cat("  • Attend beginner yoga classes on campus\n")
      cat("  • Practice 20-30 min, 3× per week minimum\n")
      cat("  • Combine physical + mental stress relief\n")
      
    } else if (mechanism == "Travelling") {
      cat("  • Plan weekend getaways or day trips\n")
      cat("  • Explore nearby nature spots or attractions\n")
      cat("  • Budget-friendly: hiking, camping, road trips\n")
      
    } else if (mechanism == "Social Media Engagement") {
      cat("  • Use for positive connections (not passive scrolling)\n")
      cat("  • Join supportive online communities\n")
      cat("  • Limit to 2-3 hours daily\n")
    }
    
    cat("\n\n")
    
    recommendations[[i]] <- list(
      rank = i,
      mechanism = mechanism,
      confidence = rec$best_confidence,
      lift = rec$best_lift,
      match_score = rec$best_match_score,
      evidence_count = rec$total_evidence,
      matching_conditions = rec$best_matching_conditions
    )
  }
  
  # -----------------------------------
  # STEP 6: ADDITIONAL SUPPORT
  # -----------------------------------
  
  if (predicted_stress >= 7) {
    cat("========================================\n")
    cat("⚠️  HIGH STRESS ALERT\n")
    cat("========================================\n\n")
    cat("Your predicted stress level is HIGH. Please consider:\n")
    cat("  • Speaking with a campus counselor\n")
    cat("  • Attending mental health workshops\n")
    cat("  • Using crisis helplines if needed\n\n")
  }
  
  # Return results
  return(list(
    predicted_stress = predicted_stress,
    stress_category = stress_category,
    stress_drivers = stress_factors,
    matched_rules_count = sum(matched_rules$match_score > 0.5),
    recommendations = recommendations
  ))
}
```

```{r}
validate_recommendation_system <- function(test_data, 
                                          association_rules_df,
                                          regression_model) {
  #' Validate the recommendation system
  #' 
  #' @param test_data: test dataset
  #' @param association_rules_df: association rules
  #' @param regression_model: trained model
  #' 
  #' @return: validation metrics
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("RECOMMENDATION SYSTEM VALIDATION\n")
  cat("========================================\n\n")
  
  # 1. Prediction accuracy
  predictions <- predict(regression_model, newdata = test_data)
  rmse <- sqrt(mean((test_data$mental_stress_level - predictions)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
  mae <- mean(abs(test_data$mental_stress_level - predictions), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  cat("STRESS PREDICTION ACCURACY:\n")
  cat("  RMSE:", round(rmse, 3), "\n")
  cat("  MAE:", round(mae, 3), "\n")
  cat("  Average error:", round(mae, 2), "points on 1-10 scale\n\n")
  
  # 2. Classification accuracy (stress categories)
  test_data$predicted_stress <- predictions
  test_data$predicted_category <- case_when(
    predictions <= 3 ~ "Low",
    predictions <= 6 ~ "Medium",
    predictions <= 10 ~ "High"
  )
  
  confusion_matrix <- table(Actual = test_data$stress_category, 
                            Predicted = test_data$predicted_category)
  
  cat("STRESS CATEGORY CLASSIFICATION:\n")
  print(confusion_matrix)
  
  accuracy <- sum(diag(confusion_matrix)) / sum(confusion_matrix)
  cat("\nOverall Accuracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 1), "%\n\n")
  
  # 3. Check if recommended coping mechanisms align with effective ones
  cat("RECOMMENDATION QUALITY ASSESSMENT:\n")
  
  # Get top recommended mechanisms from rules
  top_mechanisms <- association_rules_df %>%
    arrange(desc(lift)) %>%
    head(10) %>%
    pull(coping_mechanism) %>%
    unique()
  
  cat("Top recommended mechanisms (by lift):\n")
  for (i in seq_along(top_mechanisms)) {
    cat("  ", i, ".", top_mechanisms[i], "\n")
  }
  
  # 4. Coverage - how many students can we provide recommendations for?
  cat("\nSYSTEM COVERAGE:\n")
  cat("  Total association rules:", nrow(association_rules_df), "\n")
  cat("  Rules with lift > 5:", sum(association_rules_df$lift > 5), "\n")
  cat("  Rules with confidence > 0.8:", sum(association_rules_df$confidence > 0.8), "\n")
  
  # 5. Recommendation diversity
  all_mechanisms <- association_rules_df$coping_mechanism %>% unique()
  cat("\nRECOMMENDATION DIVERSITY:\n")
  cat("  Unique coping mechanisms recommended:", length(all_mechanisms), "\n")
  cat("  Mechanisms:", paste(all_mechanisms, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")
  
  return(list(
    rmse = rmse,
    mae = mae,
    accuracy = accuracy,
    confusion_matrix = confusion_matrix,
    top_mechanisms = top_mechanisms
  ))
}

# Run validation
validation_results <- validate_recommendation_system(
  test_data = test_data,
  association_rules_df = stress_rules_df,
  regression_model = model_step
)

# STEP 5.13: CROSS-VALIDATION

cat("CROSS-VALIDATION ANALYSIS\n")
cat("========================================\n\n")

# Perform k-fold cross-validation
library(caret)

# Train model with cross-validation
cv_model <- train(mental_stress_level ~ 
                    age + gender + academic_performance_gpa + 
                    study_hours_per_week + social_media_usage_hours_per_day +
                    sleep_duration_hours_per_night + physical_exercise_hours_per_week +
                    family_support + financial_stress + peer_pressure +
                    relationship_stress + diet_quality + cognitive_distortions +
                    substance_use + counseling_attendance + 
                    family_mental_health_history + medical_condition +
                    stress_coping_mechanisms,
                  data = stress_survey_data,
                  method = "lm",
                  trControl = train_control)

print(cv_model)

cat("Cross-Validation R²:", round(cv_model$results$Rsquared, 3), "\n")
```
